title: Misleading hints harmed other traffic and quality equivalence remained unproved
summary: Enabled-without-hints QA throughput was 0.9667 of ARC (95% interval 0.9539–0.9797), leaving the declared 3% loss bound unresolved. Misleading hints increased unhinted first-token latency beyond the declared bound. Aggregate throughput concealed interference, and output audits retained factual, format and truncation failures.
scope: Fresh QA: 24 pairs. Misleading-advice study: four advice blocks. Objective checks covered 10,616 primary and 3,504 addendum finals, with selected source reviews.
limitations: Failure-selected review is not population accuracy. Per-process unhinted p99 had only sixteen requests. Completed workflows and served tokens are not correctness-adjusted utility.
decision: Require separate overhead, unhinted-traffic and output-validity accounting when interpreting future performance.

chart.caption: Four misleading-advice blocks; original 95% interval. Above 1 is slower. The observed increase exceeded the declared 5% bound.
